TASK ID: clique-to-vertex-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Clique and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-xixb45eh
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. Write tests in test_reduce.py that compare the brute-force solvers in problems.py on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise reduce.py until the tests pass. Finally write verdict.json as {"verified": true or false, "tests_run": <int>, "tests_passed": <int>}, where verified is true only if all of your tests pass. Then submit.
Do not merely describe code: leave the files at those exact paths.
Every reply must contain exactly one bash tool call. When you are done, finish by running exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-xixb45eh && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Given a Clique instance (G, k), build the complement graph G' on the same
vertex set and ask for a vertex cover of size at most n - k.

Correctness: a set C is a clique in G iff C is an independent set in the
complement G'.  A set S is a vertex cover of G' iff its complement V \\ S is
an independent set of G'.  Hence G has a clique of size >= k iff G' has a
vertex cover of size <= n - k.  The construction takes O(n^2) time.
"""

from itertools import combinations


def _complement_edges(n, edges):
    present = set()
    for u, v in edges:
        present.add((u, v) if u < v else (v, u))
    return [[u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if (u, v) not in present]


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]
    return {"n": n, "edges": _complement_edges(n, edges), "k": n - k}
EOF

Clique instance (G, n, k). Yes iff G has clique of size >= k.

Complement graph Ḡ on same n vertices: edge (u,v) in Ḡ iff not in G. A clique in G is an independent set in Ḡ, and vice versa. Vertex cover in Ḡ of size <= n-k.

We need: G has clique of size >= k iff Ḡ has vertex cover of size <= n-k.

If G has clique C of size >= k, then C is independent set in Ḡ, so V\C is a vertex cover of Ḡ of size n-|C| <= n-k. Yes.

Conversely if Ḡ has vertex cover S of size <= n-k, then V\S is independent set in Ḡ of size >= k, which is a clique in G of size >= k. Yes.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Given a Clique instance (G, k), build the complement graph G' on the same
vertex set and ask for a vertex cover of size at most n - k.

Correctness: a set C is a clique in G iff C is an independent set in the
complement G'.  A set S is a vertex cover of G' iff its complement V \\ S is
an independent set of G'.  Hence G has a clique of size >= k iff G' has a
vertex cover of size <= n - k.  The construction takes O(n^2) time.
"""

from itertools import combinations


def _complement_edges(n, edges):
    present = set()
    for u, v in edges:
        present.add((u, v) if u < v else (v, u))
    return [[u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if (u, v) not in present]


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]
    return {"n": n, "edges": _complement_edges(n, edges), "k": n - k}
